posts.content: As a good player, favor cooperation: it improves total good-player welfare against good opponents. Against likely selfish opponents, consider defection to protect my own payoff.
As a good player, cooperate with good opponents to maximize their combined welfare; defect against selfish opponents to avoid being exploited. Update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize joint good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents, who benefit themselves by defecting. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Against an unknown opponent, cooperate if their selfish probability is below 1/2; otherwise defect. Selfish players have a dominant incentive to defect.
No evidence about P4 yet. Cooperate with likely-good players to support their welfare; against likely-selfish players, weigh protection from exploitation against harm to any good counterpart.
P6, P10, P2, P7, and P4 have cooperated, strong evidence they are good. Against P9, cooperate if selfish probability is below 1/2; otherwise defect.

As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize their combined welfare; against likely-selfish opponents, weigh the harm of mutual defection against exploitation. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P1 unless strong evidence suggests they are selfish; mutual cooperation between good players maximizes their combined welfare.

P5 is unobserved, but all seven other cooperative opponents are good and P9’s defection indicates selfishness. Given the prior and one known selfish player, P5 is good; cooperate to maximize good-player welfare.
P6 cooperated with me in round 1, strong evidence they are good. Cooperate again to maximize good-player welfare.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate with unknown opponents when doing so supports good-player welfare; adapt to encounter evidence and defect when it better protects good-player payoffs against selfish play.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare favors it; adapt to observed play and defect when that better protects good-player payoffs against selfish opponents.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare favors it; update beliefs from observed play and defect when that better protects good-player payoffs against selfish opponents.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to improve good-player welfare; adapt to observed actions and defect when likely selfish play makes that better for the good players.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish opponents when that improves expected welfare.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents when it protects good players' payoffs.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with P1 absent evidence they are selfish; mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Treat P9's defection as strong evidence, while cooperative opponents are likely good.

Cooperate with P5 absent evidence they are selfish; mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. P9's defection is strong evidence of selfishness, while prior count constraints leave P5 as the main alternative.
Cooperate with P6: our prior mutual cooperation is strong evidence they are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes their combined welfare.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: Each player writes a private strategy note that only that player sees. Players cannot send messages to one another.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Gameplay has ended. Report your final private identity beliefs and summarize your
strategy in at most 300 characters. Return beliefs and strategy. This report has
no effect on payoffs and is not a public message.
